result.title: BEND: Spectral Bregman Losses for Multi-Image Unlearning in Diffusion Models
result.summary: Diffusion models memorize training images and reproduce them almost verbatim when prompted, creating copyright and privacy liabilities. Data unlearning erases the influence of specific training samples from a trained model without retraining, and is two-sided: it must forget the targets while preserving generation quality on everything else. Prior methods use the squared-L2 diffusion loss, at most with a hand-set frequency mask; however, it is known that every Bregman divergence is a mathematically valid choice and the squared-L2 is only the simplest example. BEND is the first to search this family: it fits a spectral Bregman divergence to the unlearning task through a bilevel loop, so the loss itself is shaped to forget thoroughly while protecting quality. It also redirects a memorized image to the mean of its retain images, where ReTrack, the state of the art, redirects it to a single near-copy. On Stable Diffusion, a single BEND model erases all 48 verifiably memorized benchmark images at once. It forgets at least as much as per-target, sequential, and jointly trained ReTrack (SSCD 0.084 versus 0.094-0.120), at the quality of the model before unlearning (CLIP-IQA 0.81 versus 0.64-0.69). BEND also outperforms the state of the art on CelebA-HQ in all three measures of the benchmark, and matches or exceeds it on MNIST and CIFAR-10.

AI.brief_summary: 该论文提出 BEND，在扩散模型的多图像遗忘任务中通过双层循环搜索谱域 Bregman 散度损失，并把记忆图像重定向到保留集均值，以兼顾遗忘彻底性与生成质量。
AI.relevance_reason: 研究目标是图像生成模型的版权与隐私遗忘及生成质量保持，不涉及多模态推理中的视觉细节保留、latent 状态生成或证据使用，其损失谱搜索也服务于分布遗忘而非推理监督，缺少可核查的具体联系。
